idiom_name: fallible associated function (try_new / from_*) returning Result<Self, E>; TryFrom for rehydration
implementation_notes: Rust has no constructors and no exceptions, so the factory is an associated function with a domain name that validates and returns Result<Self, E> - keep new() infallible and add try_new/parse/from_* for the checked path - and private fields make it mandatory, because a struct literal is impossible outside the module that defines them. What replaces the classic factory class is the associated function plus the module boundary; implement TryFrom<Row> so rehydration composes with ?, and use a separate factory struct only when creation must hold trait objects (repositories, policies) at run time.
pitfalls: panic! inside a factory turns a data error into a crash; reserve it for programmer bugs and return Err for anything that comes from outside the program.
serde's derived Deserialize builds the struct field by field and never calls try_new; deserialize into a raw DTO and convert with TryFrom, or write a custom Deserialize impl.
Code inside the defining module can still use struct literals and skip validation; keep invariant-bearing fields private to the module that owns the factory.
